# Adding business days

Implement `add_business_days(start, n, holidays=())` in `solution.py`. It returns a `datetime.date`.

## Definitions

A **business day** is a Monday to Friday that is not in `holidays`.

## Behaviour

- `n > 0`: move forward from `start` and return the date of the `n`-th business day **after** `start`. `start` itself is never counted, whether or not it is a business day.
- `n < 0`: the same, moving backward: return the `|n|`-th business day **before** `start`.
- `n == 0`: return `start` if it is a business day; otherwise return the **next** business day after it.

## Inputs

- `start` must be a `datetime.date` and not a `datetime.datetime`; otherwise raise `TypeError`.
- `n` must be an `int`; `bool` and `float` raise `TypeError`.
- `holidays` is any iterable of `datetime.date` values (list, set, tuple, generator). An element that is not a `date`, or that is a `datetime`, raises `TypeError`. Holidays that fall on a weekend change nothing.

I implemented `add_business_days` in `solution.py` following `spec.md`, and wrote 40 pytest tests in `tests/test_solution.py`. `python -m pytest -q tests` passes all 40. One test expectation was wrong on my first run (Thursday plus two business days is Monday, not Tuesday), so I fixed the test, not the code.

The implementation converts `holidays` into a set once, then walks day by day in the direction of `n`, counting only Monday–Friday dates that aren't holidays. `n == 0` returns `start` if it is a business day, otherwise the next one. Type checks reject `datetime` (and `bool`/`float`) before any work is done. The tests cover forward and backward moves, year boundaries, weekend and holiday starts, weekend holidays, all iterable kinds for `holidays`, and every `TypeError` case.

I did not run coverage, mutation testing, CRAP or bandit, since the only shell command allowed was the test run. By inspection every branch is exercised, and the code has no obvious security issues, but those gates are unverified.
